title: 10 climbers, led by Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja missing after avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak - theweek.in
description: 10 climbers, led by Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja missing after avalanche on Pakistan's Broad Peak  theweek.in
publisher.title: theweek.in
full_article:
A group of 10 international climbers led by a Nepali mountaineer, Nirmal Purja, is feared missing after an avalanche struck the team late Thursday at the Broad Peak, one of the highest mountains in northern Pakistan.

The vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, Karrar Haidiri, said that the climbers have been out of communication since then.

The expedition included five Nepalese climbers, Nepal-born British mountaineer Nirmal Purja, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi of Hunzqa, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis and a Chinese climber Wang. The group also included an unidentified foreign climber, according to Haidiri.

The Pakistan Alpine Club said that the avalanche struck the 8,047-meter-high Broad Peak in the Karakoram Range around noon Thursday.

The accident occurred when the team was on an expedition to the peak.

The Alpine club has found that the tracking device Nirmal Purja carried showed movement, raising hopes for the rescue teams.

The device’s location has changed after the avalanche, according to Purja’s business partner and Nepal MP Mingma Gyaby Sherpa.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” the club said.

"We are coordinating with the authorities and trying to arrange a helicopter rescue on Friday morning Pakistani time, depending on weather conditions," Haidri told the BBC.

Purja, 43, also known as Nims Dai, has broken multiple climbing records since he became a full-time mountaineer and tour guide in 2018 after leaving the British Military.

He climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders”, peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet, in six months and six days between April and October 2019, breaking a record that year.

Purja was also part of a team of nine other Nepalese climbers who completed the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021.

Purja had also previously joined the British Army in 2003 and became a Royal Marine in 2009.

पाकिस्तान अल्पाइन क्लब के कहनाय छनि जे गुरुवार के दुपहर के करीब काराकोरम रेंज के 8047 मीटर ऊँच ब्रॉड पीक पर हिमस्खलन भेल छल.

ई दुर्घटना तखन भेल जखन टीम चोटी पर पहुँचबाक अभियान पर छल।

अल्पाइन क्लब न॑ पालै छै कि निर्मल पुरजा के साथ जे ट्रैकिंग डिवाइस छेलै, ओकरा म॑ हलचल देखलऽ गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा स॑ बचाव टीमऽ लेली उम्मीद बढ़ी गेलऽ छै ।

पुरजा केरऽ बिजनेस पार्टनर आरू नेपाल केरऽ सांसद मिंगमा ग्याबी शेर्पा के अनुसार हिमस्खलन के बाद डिवाइस केरऽ स्थान बदली गेलऽ छै ।

क्लब नँ कहलकै, “हर संभव प्रयास करलौ जाय रहलौ छै कि हेलीकॉप्टर सपोर्ट आरू सब उपलब्ध बचाव संसाधन क ​​मौसम आरू परिचालन के स्थिति के आधार प जल्दी स॑ जल्दी मौका प॑ जुटान करलऽ जाय ।

हैदरी न॑ बीबीसी क॑ बतैलकै कि हम्में अधिकारियऽ के साथ समन्वय करी रहलऽ छियै आरू मौसम के हिसाब स॑ शुक्रवार के सुबह पाकिस्तानी समय प॑ हेलीकॉप्टर स॑ बचाव के व्यवस्था करै के कोशिश करी रहलऽ छियै ।

43 वर्षीय पुर्जा, जेकरा निम्स दाई के नाम स॑ भी जानलऽ जाय छै, न॑ ब्रिटिश मिलिट्री छोड़ला के बाद २०१८ म॑ पूर्णकालिक पर्वतारोही आरू टूर गाइड बनला के बाद स॑ कईएक पर्वतारोही रिकॉर्ड तोड़ी चुकलऽ छै ।

अप्रैल आरू अक्टूबर २०१९ के बीच छह महीना आरू छह दिन म॑ हुनी सब १४ “आठ-हजार”, ८,००० मीटर यानी २६,००० फीट स॑ ऊपर के चोटी प॑ चढ़ी क॑ वू साल एगो रिकॉर्ड तोड़ी देलकै ।

पुरजा 2021 मे के2 के पहिल शीतकालीन आरोहण पूरा करय वाला नौ अन्य नेपाली पर्वतारोही के टीम के हिस्सा सेहो छल.

पुरजा सेहो एहि सं पहिने 2003 मे ब्रिटिश सेना मे शामिल भ गेल छलाह आओर 2009 मे रॉयल मरीन बनल छलाह.

title: Pakistan rescuers find 4 bodies of the 10 climbers missing on Broad Peak after an avalanche - The New Indian Express
description: Pakistan rescuers find 4 bodies of the 10 climbers missing on Broad Peak after an avalanche  The New Indian Express
publisher.title: The New Indian Express
full_article:
ISLAMABAD: Rescuers searching for 10 climbers missing after an avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak located four bodies Friday and were continuing to search for the other six, officials said.

Efforts were underway to retrieve the bodies of the four climbers despite the harsh weather, according to the senior government officials. The officials, who spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media, did not immediately identify whose bodies were found.

“The team has been out of communication since Thursday,” said Karrar Haidri, vice president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan, who said army helicopters had joined the search-and-rescue operation and authorities were in contact with the families of the missing climbers.

According to the Alpine Club, the expedition included five Nepali climbers, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi from Hunza, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and another foreign climber.

The expedition leader was the renowned moutaineer Nirmal Purja, a Nepal-born former soldier in the British army widely known as Nims Dai. He climbed the world’s 14 highest peaks in a record 189 days in 2019, an achievement featured in the Netflix documentary, “14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible.” His record was surpassed in 2023.

Moving Mountains, a travel company based in Pakistan, announced late last month that the expedition team was on its way to the small town of Askole and wished them a safe journey climbing Broad Peak. The company said this was Geis’ first try at an 8,000-meter peak in Pakistan, while it was expected to be Sakhi’s final one.

अल्पाइन क्लब के अनुसार ई अभियान में पांच नेपाली पर्वतारोही, हुन्जा के पाकिस्तानी पर्वतारोही सोहेल सखी, ओमानी पर्वतारोही नाथिरा, अमेरिकी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेइस, चीनी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस, जेकरऽ पहचान केवल वांग के नाम स॑ करलऽ गेलऽ छै, आरू एगो आरू विदेशी पर्वतारोही शामिल छेलै ।

अभियान केरऽ नेता छेलै प्रसिद्ध माउंटेनर निर्मल पुरजा, जे नेपाल म॑ जन्मलऽ ब्रिटिश सेना केरऽ पूर्व सैनिक छेलै जेकरा व्यापक रूप स॑ निम्स दाई के नाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय छै । 2019 म॑ रिकॉर्ड 189 दिन म॑ दुनिया केरऽ 14 सबसें उच्च चोटी प॑ चढ़ी गेलऽ छेलै, जेकरा नेटफ्लिक्स केरऽ डॉक्यूमेंट्री, “14 चोटी: नथिंग इज इम्पॉसिबल” म॑ पेश करलऽ गेलऽ उपलब्धि छै । हुनकर रिकॉर्ड 2023 मे पार भ गेल छल।

Previous deaths on Broad Peak published at 09:43 BST 09:43 BST Image source, AFP via Getty Images The first successful ascent of Broad Peak was in 1957, when a four-member Austrian expedition reached the summit. Since then, many more have climbed the 8,051m (26,414 ft) peak. And dozens have lost their lives to the mountain. 2013 marked one of Broad Peak's deadliest years, with at least six fatalities recorded. That March, two Polish climbers - aged 27 and 58 - were declared dead after they went missing during their descent from the summit. A few months later three Iranian climbers suffered a similar fate, and a German climber died after she slipped and was swept away by a mountain stream. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing China urgently working to verify information - foreign ministry published at 09:13 BST 09:13 BST China's foreign ministry has said it is urgently working to verify details of the situation at Broad Peak. One Chinese national is among the 10 climbers who lost contact after an avalanche on Thursday. The Chinese ministry has said it would provide help according to Pakistan's needs. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Other big mountaineering names also among the missing published at 08:39 BST 08:39 BST Pradeep Bashyal

BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Besides Nirmal Purja, there are a few other big names among the missing climbers, including Pur Bahadur Gurung - also known as Yukta - and Kili Pemba Sherpa. Yukta is certified by the International Federation of Mountain Guides Associations (IFMGA), and is very close to completing the 14 peaks challenge, where climbers attempt to summit the world's 14 mountains that rise at least 8,000m above sea level. Just last spring Yukta summited Nepal’s three "eight-thousanders", and by the end of that season had 10 Everest ascents and 12 eight-thousanders to his name. He was also part of the team that discovered a century-old shoe with the inscription "A.C. Irvine", believed to be of British climber Andrew "Sandy" Irvine, who vanished on Everest with George Mallory in 1924. Kili Pemba has so far summited Everest 15 times. In 2021 he was a member of a historic K2 winter expedition, alongwith several Nepali climbers including Nirmal Purja. Kili Pemba is also the guide who led double amputee Xia Boyu to summit Everest in 2018. Xia, a Chinese climber, had lost both legs decades earlier while attempting to reach Everest's summit. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Climbers' GPS trackers provide clues published at 08:15 BST 08:15 BST As the search operation is under way, GPS data from the missing climbers' trackers provide clues on what happened when the avalanche hit Broad Peak. Samson Sharaf, the mentor of one of the 10 missing climbers, shared GPS data to industry website Climbing which indicate that the avalanche hit between 08:57 and 09:30 local time. At that time, American climber Mallory Geis, according to her GPS tracker, descended by 543m (1,781ft) while Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy decended by 1,651m (5,417ft). Earlier, we reported that the tracking device belonging to Nirmal Purja had been showing movement. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing A nervous wait for updates from the avalanche site published at 07:48 BST 07:48 BST Carrie Davies

BBC Pakistan correspondent Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Broad Peak (in the background of this shot) is a notorious climbing route The search-and-rescue operation looking for 10 climbers missing in the Karakorum mountains has detected the location of four of their trackers - although they cannot identify if the climbers they belong to are dead or alive, according to the General Secretary of Pakistan’s Alpine club. The 10 climbers include renowned Nepal-born former British special forces soldier Nirmal Purja. All were climbing Broad Peak, the world’s 12th-highest mountain, when an avalanche struck. It is a nervous wait as rescuers try to reach the four climbers' location. Ayaz Shigri, general secretary of Pakistan Alpine Club, said that while the trackers had been located, there has been no movement from them. The rescue operation continues with drones and a ground team. Military helicopters are also on the way, and currently at the K2 base camp, according to Shigri. He estimated it to be a four-hour climb to reach the location of the four trackers with oxygen support. He hoped there would be more clarity by early evening, but said they did not know about the location of the other six climbers. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Where is Broad Peak? published at 07:25 BST 07:25 BST Broad Peak is the twelfth tallest mountain on Earth and the third tallest in the Karakoram Range. Its name comes from its unusually long summit ridge, which extends for about 2 kilometers. There had been a total of 404 successful ascents of Broad Peak as of March 2012, while 21 climbers had died trying - a fatality rate of about 5 percent, said Nasa. Image source, Getty Images Image source, Getty Images Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Three trackers located, local officials say published at 07:15 BST 07:15 BST Local officials have told BBC Urdu that three trackers have been located at altitudes ranging from approximately 6,000m to 7,000m. Mountaineers usually carry GPS tracking devices when they climb major peaks. In 2024, the Nepali government made it mandatory for Mount Everest climbers to carry such trackers. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing All six mountaineers still ‘missing’, says Nepal government published at 06:55 BST 06:55 BST Pradeep Bashyal

BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Nepal’s Tourism Department has issued a statement saying it has instructed the country's embassy in Islamabad to coordinate with the Pakistan government in rescue efforts. Despite reports of multiple bodies having been found, the Department did not confirm any deaths - naming the six Nepalis from the expedition as "missing". Nepali companies based across several mountains in Pakistan are preparing to go to the scene and work with local authorities, it added. Department spokesperson Himal Gautam told the BBC: "There is a significant presence of Nepali Sherpas and expedition companies who are coordinating among themselves." "This is an unprecedented incident," Gautam added. "However, there are still some tiny hopes, with some conflicting information." Medhavi Gulati, a researcher on Sherpa and high-altitude mountaineering who is a lecturer at Panjab University says Nepal’s Sherpas are the most efficient highly-skilled staff when it comes to professional guiding. "Sherpas are highly preferred over local guides in because of their long history of high-altitude mountaineering and their professional training across diverse mountain environments." Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Pakistan’s mountains: the second major job market for Nepal’s Sherpas published at 06:38 BST 06:38 BST Pradeep Bashyal

BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Pakistan’s mountains have gained popularity as more and more people attempt to complete the 14 Peaks: the challenge of climbing all fourteen of the world's mountains that rise higher than 8,000 metres. Of these fourteen peaks, five are climbed from Pakistan, two from China (including Everest, which is also climbed from Nepal), and eight from Nepal. Nepal’s Sherpas, renowned for their mountain-guiding expertise, spend most of the spring climbing season working on Nepal’s high mountains. As the monsoon arrives in Nepal, many go to Pakistan for its climbing season before returning home for Nepal’s autumn expeditions. “The recently growing prestige of completing all 14 peaks has made Pakistan’s mountains the second major workplace for Nepal’s Sherpas,” says Khimlal Gautam, a Nepali mountaineer and author. “However, Sherpas are equally sought after across the world - from the mountains of Europe and the Americas, to Antarctica.” Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Four bodies found by rescue teams, says Alpine club president published at 06:29 BST 06:29 BST Breaking As many as four bodies have been recovered by ground rescue teams, president of the Alpine Club of Pakistan Irfan Arshad Khan has said in a post on Instagram. The BBC is unable to independently verify this. Earlier, we reported that Nepal's Ambassador to Pakistan, Rita Dhital, said she had acknowledged that there were reports of bodies found on the scene but said she had not received hat there was no official confirmation. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Search under way for missing mountaineers published at 06:22 BST 06:22 BST The seach for the missing mountaineers on Broad Peak is under way, our teams on the ground in Pakistan can confirm. In an interview with Nepali news outlet Kantipur, Nepali Ambassador to Pakistan Rita Dhital says an aerial and ground search effort has been mobilised. Dhital says the aerial search involves helicopters and drones and acknowledged that there are unconfirmed reports of bodies found on the scene, but added that there was no official confirmation yet. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 14 Peaks: Nirmal Purja's mountaineering record published at 06:08 BST 06:08 BST Image source, AFP via Getty Images Nirmal Purja, known as Nims Dai, holds multiple mountaineering records. But his most famous feat was set in 2019, when he climbed the world’s 14 tallest peaks in just six months - the shortest amount of time anyone has done that. The previous record for such a feat stood at nearly eight years. This journey, named Project Possible, was captured in the documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing is Impossible. As he approached the peak of Everest in May 2019, he snapped a photo of a snaking queue of climbers all waiting to summit The traffic jam photo went viral and sparked a conversation about dangerous overcrowding on the world’s tallest peak. The message he said he hoped to send with his ambitious mission was that anyone could achieve their dreams if they put their minds to it. "It's not about mountain climbing, it's about following your goals," he previously told the BBC. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing What you need to know published at 05:53 BST 05:53 BST A group of mountaineers, including renowned Nepali-born climber Nirmal Purja are feared missing on Broad Peak, the world's 12th highest mountain. Here's what you need to know: The search will start as soon as the weather permits and the Pakistan Army has dispatched two helicopters

Purja is the leader of the expedition. He is famed for climbing all 14 of the world's 8,000-metre plus mountains in just over six months in 2019

The avalanche struck late on Thursday and the group has not been contacted since

Nepali media report two bodies have been found and have yet to be identified We'll bring you the latest updates as we get them - stay with us. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Nepali and Pakistani alpine clubs coordinating rescue efforts published at 05:30 BST 05:30 BST Pradeep Bashyal

BBC Nepali, Kathmandu Nepal's Mountaineering Association (NMA) is currently coordinating with the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) in its rescue efforts, says Rajendra Bahadur Lama, General Secretary of NMA. "Some of our Sherpa friends based in K2 are going there for rescue efforts," he said, adding that there were reports that some mountaineers had been spotted from rescue helicopters, though this cannot be confirmed. The 10 climbers on the mountain are made up of guides and their foreign clients from three Nepali companies - Elite Exped, Seven Summit Treks and Imagine Nepal. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Two bodies found after avalanche - report published at 05:21 BST 05:21 BST Nepali news outlet Kantipur is reporting now that two bodies of two climbers have been found at the scene. Thaneshwar Guragain, general manager of hiking agency Seven Summit Treks, told Kantipur that an identification process was underway. When asked about the possibility of finding other climbers alive, Guragain said their chanes were "slim", adding "the space for hope has become very narrow". Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Who was on the expedition team? published at 05:15 BST 05:15 BST The Alpine Club has released the names of the 10 climbers who are missing after the avalanche on Broad Peak: Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy (Oman) Sohail Sakhi (Pakistan) Wang Zhong (China) Mallory Geis (US) Nirmal Purja "Nims Dai" (Nepal) Pur Bahadur Gurung "Yukta" (Nepal) Kili Pemba Sherpa "Kilu" (Nepal) Nima Sherpa (Nepal) Nawang Thindu Sherpa (Nepal) Gyalu Sherpa (Nepal) Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Pakistan Army sends two rescue helicopters published at 05:01 BST 05:01 BST Carrie Davies

BBC Pakistan correspondent It's just past 9am in Pakistan and two army rescue helicopters carrying rescue personnel and additional specialised equipment have been dispatched to support the ongoing search and rescue operation, the country's Alpine Club has told me. The helicopters are reinforcing efforts on the ground to assist the stranded climbers and enhance the effectiveness of the operation in the challenging high-altitude environment, they added. The Alpine Club also said they sincerely appreciated the prompt response and unwavering support of the Pakistan Army Aviation and all agencies involved and they remained hopeful for the safe recovery of the missing climbers and would continue to provide updates Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Climbers deployed from other mountains to help with search - Nepal lawmaker published at 04:47 BST 04:47 BST Koh Ewe

Live reporter Climbers on other mountains in the region have been deployed to help with search efforts on Broad Peak, a Nepalese lawmaker has just told the BBC. Climbers in K2 and K3, two nearby mountains in the Karakoram range are descending from their camps to help with search efforts, says Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, a Nepalese lawmaker. He's also a business associate of Nirmal Purja. Members of Imagine Nepal, a commercial mountaineering operator, are also helping out, he says. Earlier we reported that movement had been recorded on Purja's tracking device - Mingma Gyabu Sherpa has confirmed this to the BBC as well, though he adds that this movement was recorded in the tracking system yesterday. Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing What is Broad Peak? published at 04:42 BST 04:42 BST Image source, Getty Images Broad Peak in Pakistan is regarded as one of the more challenging mountains for expeditions, and is ranked as the world's 12th highest peak. It's summit is 8,047m (26,400ft) high. That is also where yesterday's avalanche occured, in the Karakoram range, according to Pakistani authorities. It is among 14 "death zone" peaks that Nirmal Purja climbed in just over six months in 2019. In 2022, Broad Peak was the subject of an eponymous Netflix film that told the story of how a Polish climber attempted the first winter ascent to the mountain's peak. Image source, International Space Station Image caption, Photo from the International Space Station shows Broad Peak as seen from space Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing Nirmal Purja's tracker appears active - report published at 04:21 BST 04:21 BST The tracking device belonging to Nirmal Purja has reportedly been showing movement, according to a report by Nepali newspaper Kantipur. The device's position has been changing in the tracking system, Mingma Gyabu Sherpa, Nirmal Purja's business partner, told Kantipur. He also said that even though the avalanche happened in the day on Thursday, they only got detailed information of it in the evening. We'll bring you more updates as we get them. title: Nepali journalist Anup Ojha wins Developing Asia Journalism Award - The Kathmandu Post
description: Nepali journalist Anup Ojha wins Developing Asia Journalism Award  The Kathmandu Post
publisher.title: The Kathmandu Post
full_article:
Nepali journalist Anup Ojha, a correspondent for Agence France-Presse (AFP), has won second prize at the Developing Asia Journalism Awards (DAJA) 2026 for his report on Nepal’s use of artificial intelligence to strengthen landslide early warning systems. Ojha previously worked for The Kathmandu Post.

Ojha was recognised for his story, “Landslide-prone Nepal Tests AI-powered Warning System”, which examined Nepal’s efforts to deploy AI technology to predict landslides and provide at-risk communities with warnings during the monsoon season.

Organised by the Asian Development Bank Institute (ADBI), the awards honour journalism that sheds light on development challenges and innovative solutions across Asia. This year’s competition drew 79 entries from 17 countries, with a focus on how artificial intelligence is transforming economies, public services and daily life.

Ojha shared the second prize with Guinevere Latoza of the Philippine Centre for Investigative Journalism, whose investigation explored how the rapid expansion of data centres is affecting energy-burdened households in the Philippines.

The first prize was awarded jointly to Indonesian journalists Roni Satria of CNN Indonesia for “AI and Dietary Colonisation: When Nasi Uduk Is Considered a Sin” and Caecilia Mediana of Kompas for “Fate of Digital Platform Shadow Workers”. Khulan M. of Inside Mongolia received an honourable mention for “Can AI Strengthen Mongolia's Disaster Prevention?”

According to ADBI, the judging panel of journalists and researchers selected five winning entries. Each winner will receive a cash prize of $2,000, with the awards ceremony to be held online in August.

Ojha’s story highlighted both the promise and the challenges of applying AI in one of the world's most landslide-prone countries, where extreme monsoon rainfall, fragile terrain and climate change continue to increase disaster risks.

title: Missing climber Nirmal Purja redefined mountaineering - France 24
description: Missing climber Nirmal Purja redefined mountaineering  France 24
publisher.title: France 24
full_article:
Purja, 43, served with Britain's Brigade of Gurkhas and then the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines before becoming a full-time mountaineer and guide.

In 2019, he famously completed the summit of the 14 highest peaks in the world in just over six months, shattering the previous record of seven years.

The determined climber had the 14 mountains tattooed across his back, complete with swirling clouds and Tibetan prayer flags.

His efforts were chronicled in a 2021 Netflix documentary, inspiring a new wave of climbers.

But Purja has also faced criticism for his use of guides, oxygen and fixed ropes, as well as helicopters to go from one base camp to another.

In 2021, Purja made history with the first winter ascent of the treacherous K2, the world's second-highest peak, along with a team of nine other Nepali climbers.

Purja wrote on X this week that he was close to becoming the first person to climb all 14 "super peaks" twice without oxygen.

"Broad Peak, I ask for nothing but safe passage up and back down," he wrote.

"My purpose has never been about me. It's about what I represent. It's about showing YOU that your own mountains -- whatever they are -- are climbable."

Broad Peak, part of the Karakoram range in northern Pakistan, is the world's 12th-highest mountain and is regarded as one of the toughest and most technical climbs of all the 8,000-metre plus ascents.

- 'Everyone asks you about Everest' –

Pakistan's eight-thousanders © John SAEKI / AFP

Born in a village in western Nepal, Purja joined the Gurkhas -- a brigade of Nepalis in British army famous for their fearlessness -- in his teens.

He later served in the elite special forces as an extreme cold weather warfare specialist.

The adventurer told AFP in a 2019 interview that even a pair of flip-flops were a luxury for him when he was a child.

Known by the nickname "Nimsdai", his tryst with mountaineering began on a trek to an Everest base camp in 2012 when he summited the 6,119-metre (20,075-foot) Lobuche.

He climbed his first "8,000er" in 2014. Two years later, when a period of leave following a deployment to Afghanistan coincided with the climbing season, he made his first ascent of Everest.

"If you are from Nepal, everyone asks you about Everest. So I then used my breaks for mountaineering," he said.

Next year he was back on the mountain, leading a successful Gurkha climbing expedition and was made a member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) for his work in high-altitude mountaineering.

Later, he swapped his army boots for crampons, quitting the military after 16 years of service.

- Inspiration –

He then re-mortgaged his house to raise funds for his high-altitude, high-speed quest of the 14 highest peaks.

After his record-breaking feat, he opened a mountain expedition company, taking climbers up the highest peaks across the world every season.

He became a much sought-after guide after the Netflix documentary gave him global recognition.

In 2024, two women mountaineers accused Purja of sexual harassment and assault, which he denied.

In the 2019 interview with AFP, Purja had said he hoped his feat would inspire the next generation of Nepali climbers to break his records.

"As a Nepali, I hope my climbs put a spotlight on the talented climbers here," he said.

Nepali guides, usually ethnic Sherpas from the valleys around Everest, are the backbone of the country's lucrative climbing industry, but often do not get as much credit or accolades as international climbers.

Long relegated to supporting roles, Nepali climbers began gaining recognition in their own right as Purja's global profile shone a spotlight on their achievements.

Through his foundation, Purja funded education and mountain clean-ups. He also built a porter's house on the Everest route to provide safe housing for them.

Despite several records under his belt, Purja constantly sought new adventures.

"There are always (new) boundaries," he told AFP.

"(That's) human, that's what we do."

उत्तरी पाकिस्तान केरऽ काराकोरम श्रृंखला केरऽ हिस्सा ब्रॉड पीक दुनिया केरऽ १२वां सबस॑ ऊँचऽ पहाड़ छेकै आरू एकरा ८,००० मीटर प्लस केरऽ सब चढ़ाई केरऽ सबस॑ कठिन आरू तकनीकी चढ़ाई म॑ स॑ एक मानलऽ जाय छै ।

- 'सब कियो एवरेस्ट के बारे में पूछैत अछि' –

पश्चिमी नेपालक एकटा गाम मे जन्मल पुरजा किशोरावस्था मे गोरखा -- ब्रिटिश सेना मे नेपालीक एकटा ब्रिगेड जे अपन निर्भीकता लेल प्रसिद्ध छल -- मे शामिल भ गेलाह |

बाद में ओ अभिजात विशेष बल में अत्यंत ठंढा मौसम युद्ध विशेषज्ञ के रूप में सेवा केलनि ।

एडवेंचरर न॑ २०१९ म॑ एएफपी क॑ देलऽ गेलऽ साक्षात्कार म॑ कहलकै कि जब॑ हुनी बच्चा छेलै त॑ हुनका लेली एक जोड़ी फ्लिप-फ्लॉप भी एगो लग्जरी छेलै ।

"निम्सदाई) उपनाम स॑ जानलऽ जाय वाला पर्वतारोहण के साथ हुनकऽ मुलाकात २०१२ म॑ एवरेस्ट केरऽ एगो बेस कैंप केरऽ ट्रेक प॑ शुरू होलऽ छेलै जब॑ हुनी ६,११९ मीटर (२०,०७५ फीट) के लोबुचे के चोटी प॑ पहुँचलै ।

2014 में अपनऽ पहिलऽ "8,000er" चढ़लै छेलै ।दू साल बाद जब॑ अफगानिस्तान म॑ तैनाती के बाद छुट्टी के अवधि चढ़ाई के मौसम के साथ मेल खाबै छेलै, त॑ वू एवरेस्ट प॑ अपनऽ पहिलऽ चढ़ाई करलकै ।

ओ कहला जे अगर अहां नेपाल क छी त सब कियो एवरेस्ट क बारे मे पूछैत अछि, ताहि लेल हम तखन अपन ब्रेक कए पर्वतारोहण लेल उपयोग केलहुं।

अगिला साल ओ फेर सं पहाड़ पर आबि गेलाह, एकटा सफल गोर्खा पर्वतारोहण अभियान के नेतृत्व केलनि आ उच्च ऊँचाई पर पर्वतारोहण में अपन काज के लेल ऑर्डर ऑफ द ब्रिटिश साम्राज्य (एमबीई) के सदस्य बनाओल गेलाह.

बाद मे ओ अपन सेना के बूट के क्रैम्पन के संग बदलि लेलखिन्ह, 16 साल के सेवा के बाद सेना छोड़ि देलखिन्ह.

- प्रेरणा – ८.

एकरऽ बाद हुनी अपनऽ घर क॑ फेर स॑ गिरवी रखलकै ताकि १४ सबसें ऊँचऽ चोटी केरऽ अपनऽ उच्च ऊँचाई, तेज गति के खोज लेली धन जुटाबै के काम करलऽ जाय सक॑ ।

अपनऽ रिकॉर्ड तोड़ कारनामा के बाद हुनी एगो पहाड़ी अभियान कंपनी खोललकै, जे हर सीजन म॑ पर्वतारोही क॑ दुनिया भर केरऽ सबस॑ ऊँचऽ चोटी प॑ पहुँचैलकै ।

नेटफ्लिक्स केरऽ डॉक्यूमेंट्री न॑ हुनका वैश्विक पहचान देला के बाद हुनी बहुत मांग वाला गाइड बनी गेलै ।

2024 मे दूटा महिला पर्वतारोही पुरजा पर यौन उत्पीड़न आ मारपीट क आरोप लगौने छलीह, जकरा ओ खंडन केलथि।

२०१९ मे एएफपी के देल गेल साक्षात्कार मे पुरजा कहलनि छल जे हुनका उम्मीद अछि जे हुनकर ई कारनामा अगिला पीढ़ी के नेपाली पर्वतारोही के अपन रिकॉर्ड तोड़य लेल प्रेरित करत।

ओ कहलनि जे, एकटा नेपाली के रूप मे हमरा आशा अछि जे हमर चढ़ाई एहि ठामक प्रतिभाशाली पर्वतारोही पर प्रकाश डालत।

नेपाली गाइड, जे प्रायः एवरेस्टक आसपासक घाटी सं आयल जातीय शेरपा थिक, देशक आकर्षक पर्वतारोहण उद्योगक रीढ़ थिक, मुदा प्रायः अंतरराष्ट्रीय पर्वतारोही कें ओतेक श्रेय वा प्रशंसा नहिं भेटैत छैक.

बहुत दिन स सहायक भूमिका मे उतरल नेपाली पर्वतारोही कए अपनहि मे पहचान भेटय लागल, किया कि पुरजा क ग्लोबल प्रोफाइल हुनकर उपलब्धि पर चर्चा केलक।

अपनऽ फाउंडेशन के माध्यम स॑ पुरजा न॑ शिक्षा आरू पहाड़ केरऽ सफाई के फंडिंग करलकै । एवरेस्ट मार्ग पर पोर्टर के घर सेहो बनौलनि जाहि सं हुनका सभ के सुरक्षित आवास उपलब्ध कराओल जा सकय.

अपन बेल्ट के नीचा कतेको रिकॉर्ड के बावजूद पुरजा लगातार नव-नव रोमांच के तलाश में रहैत छलाह.

ओ एएफपी स कहला जे हमेशा (नव) सीमा रहैत अछि।

"(से) मनुक्ख, हम सभ त' से करैत छी।"

भारत के सीमा पर स्थित नेपाल के सुनसरी जिला के एक शहर दिवांगंज में रविदिन देर राति हिन्दू आ मुसलमान के बीच भेल झड़प में 25 गोटे घायल भ गेलाह आ अधिकारी के कहनाय छनि जे हिन्दू आयोजन के दौरान जोरदार संगीत आ धार्मिक झंडा के विवाद के कारण हिंसा शुरू भेल अछि.

रविदिन सुनसरी मे दू गोटे के गोली मारि क हत्या क देल गेल आ बृहस्पतिदिन पड़ोसी सिराहा जिला मे तेसर के मौत के खबर अछि, कारण इलाका मे छिटपुट झड़प जारी अछि। प्रहरी प्रवक्ता अबी नारायण काफ्ले कहलनि जे, घटनाक्रमक जांच चलि रहल अछि।

शुक्रदिन कोनो हिंसा नहि भेल पुलिस जनौलक अछि, मुदा कोनो तरहक दोबारा नहि होबय लेल कतेको शहर मे अनिश्चित काल धरि कर्फ्यू लगाओल गेल अछि।

नेपाल केरऽ जेन जेड समर्थित प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह न॑ गुरुवार क॑ लोगऽ स॑ शांति लेली आरू हिमालयी राष्ट्र स॑ “उथल-पुथल के बादल” दूर करै के आग्रह करलकै ।

शाह न॑ राष्ट्र क॑ देलऽ गेलऽ दुर्लभ, टेलीविजन संबोधन म॑ कहलकै कि सरकार हिंसा केरऽ निष्पक्ष आरू निष्पक्ष जांच करतै आरू परेशानी लेली जिम्मेदार लोगऽ क॑ पारदर्शी तरीका स॑ सजा देतै ।

सरकार केरऽ बयान म॑ कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि देश केरऽ गृहमंत्री सूडान गुरुंग न॑ सुनसरी म॑ मारलऽ गेलऽ दूनू के परिवार स॑ भेंट करी क॑ गुरुवार देर रात हर एक क॑ लगभग ६,६६० डॉलर के राहत दै प॑ सहमत होय गेलै ।

गुरुंग के शुक्रदिन सिराहा जा क मारल गेल तेसर व्यक्ति के परिवार सं भेंट करय के सेहो उम्मीद छल.

full_article:
Heat-related deaths in Nepal due to global warming is projected to rise by 24 deaths per 100,000 people, according to a new global study from Chicago-based Climate Impact Lab (CIL) released this week. Most at risk are people in the Tarai districts of Dhanusa, Rupandehi, and Kailali.

Nepal is among the 18 countries the report identifies as caught in a ‘Mortality Cooling Trap (MCT)’ due to lower electricity availability for fans and air conditioner to cope with the heat.

The most vulnerable to MCT is Pakistan due to its power shortage and extreme heat stress. Bangladesh and Burma are also vulnerable.

“The Mortality Cooling Trap identifies areas that are projected to see both large increases in temperature-related mortality and small changes in electricity consumption due to climate change,” explained co-author Emily Grover-Kopec. “Areas at greatest risk will not be able to adapt to heat through electric cooling.”

The CIL report covers 24,378 regions globally and measured how rising temperatures will change energy consumption worldwide, and where that will leave communities unable to adapt. They found that climate-driven temperature change would cause about 430,000 more deaths a year by 2050, with poorer countries reporting 10 times more deaths than wealthy ones.

More than 676 million people live in these trapped regions including Nepal, and the study projects about 377,000 lives lost each year from 2050 onward across these countries as a result.

POWER DOWN

In Nepal, electricity consumption could decline by 0.01 GJ per capita due to climate impact, reducing ability of 32% of the population to cope with heat stress. Load-shedding and expensive electricity would deprive many families from cooling devices.

This despite Nepal’s power generation capacity reaching 4,300MW. The government plans to generate 30,000MW by 2035, and export 10,000-15,000MW to India and Bangladesh.

Co-author Ashwin Rode of the Energy Policy Institute in Chicago notes that the projected decline in power consumption in Nepal is due to climate change, and does not look into other parameters.

“Nepal's expansion of power generation would be good news toward the goal of increasing consumption to support cooling,” Rode told Nepali Times. “But this figure was calculated based on estimated relationships between daily temperatures and energy consumption at different income levels and climatic zones.”

The report ranks the 18 Mortality Cooling Trap countries by the share of the population with electricity access. Nepal has the second-highest overall access among the 18, after Bangladesh.

CLIMATE MIGRATION

Despite being listed as one of the countries in the ‘Mortality Cooling Trap’, Nepal’s average elevation makes it relatively cooler. Besides trans-boundary migration to the mountains, within Nepal people will start moving back up to the mountains from the plains.

Preparedness for possible mass migration is lacking, and policies haven’t kept pace with mitigation and adaptation, let alone climate migration.

Warns Rode: “While migration offers a way to avoid the harms of a warming climate, it is also a costly adaptation strategy that will be particularly burdensome to the poorest, most vulnerable populations.”

URBAN HEAT ISLAND

Cooling with fans and air conditioners add to the urban heat island (UHI) effect, making core city centres up to 5°C hotter than less crowded suburbs. Heat-trapping concrete, dark asphalt surfaces, lack of vegetation and waste heat from air conditioning and vehicles add to UHI (page 9).

Already, the city core within the Ring Road in Kathmandu is up to 4°C hotter during the daytime and up to 3°C hotter in the evening than the outskirts. Green-blue spaces can lower temperatures by up to 1.2°C.

Interestingly, while 72% of the population is projected to see relatively small changes in electricity consumption due to climate change, many of those regions are not projected to see significant increases in mortality due to climate change as many are in the more mountainous areas where declines in cold-related deaths will offset any increase in heat-related deaths, notes co-author Emily Grover-Kopec of the Rhodium Group.

July 2026

MIGRATION IS A HOT TOPIC

Gaia Vince’s 2022 book Nomad Century estimated that up to 3.5 billion people will be affected by unsurvivable heat and will be on the move. Mass migration is inevitable so governments might as well get used to the idea.

Julian Hattem’s Shelter from the Storm: How Climate Change Is Creating a New Era of Migration (2026) notes that mass human displacement due to heat is already happening and plots trends into the future.

Migration and Displacement in a Changing Climate by Kelsea Best, Kayly Ober, and Robert A. McLeman (2025) examines how climate shifts interact with human societies, infrastructure, and regional adaptation measures.

Move: The Forces Uprooting Us by Parag Khanna looks at which countries people will move from and where to escape the impacts of climate change. The future will be messy.

Science fiction writer Kim Stanley Robinson’s 2019 novel The Ministry for the Future begins with the mass death of 20 million people due to a heat wave in northern India. But world governments come together to finance adaptation.

शिकागो स्थित क्लाइमेट इम्पैक्ट लैब (सीआईएल) केरऽ ई सप्ताह जारी एगो नया वैश्विक अध्ययन के अनुसार ग्लोबल वार्मिंग के कारण नेपाल म॑ गर्मी स॑ जुड़लऽ मौत म॑ प्रति एक लाख लोगऽ म॑ २४ मौत के बढ़ोत्तरी के अनुमान छै । सबसँ बेसी खतरा धनुषा, रूपन्देही, आ कैलाली के तराई जिला के लोक के अछि.

गर्मी के सामना करै लेली पंखा आरू एयर कंडीशनर के लेलऽ बिजली के उपलब्धता कम होय के कारण रिपोर्ट म॑ ‘मोर्टलिटी कूलिंग ट्रैप (एमसीटी)’ म॑ फंसलऽ १८ देशऽ म॑ नेपाल भी शामिल छै ।

एमसीटी केरऽ सबसें बेसी खतरा पाकिस्तान छै, कैन्हेंकि ओकरऽ बिजली के कमी आरू गर्मी केरऽ अत्यधिक तनाव छै । बांग्लादेश आ बर्मा सेहो कमजोर अछि।

सह-लेखिका एमिली ग्रोवर-कोपेक न॑ बतैलकै, “मॉर्टैलिटी कूलिंग ट्रैप ऐन्हऽ क्षेत्रऽ के पहचान करै छै, जेकरा म॑ तापमान स॑ जुड़लऽ मृत्यु दर म॑ बड़ऽ वृद्धि आरू जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण बिजली के खपत म॑ छोटऽ-छोटऽ बदलाव दूनू देखै के अनुमान छै । “सबसँ बेसी जोखिम वाला इलाका इलेक्ट्रिक कूलिंग के माध्यम सं गर्मी के अनुकूल नै भ सकैत अछि।”

सीआईएल केरऽ रिपोर्ट म॑ वैश्विक स्तर प॑ २४,३७८ क्षेत्रऽ क॑ शामिल करलऽ गेलऽ छै आरू ई मापलऽ गेलऽ छै कि बढ़तऽ तापमान स॑ दुनिया भर म॑ ऊर्जा के खपत म॑ कोन तरह के बदलाव आबै वाला छै, आरू ई स॑ समुदाय कहाँ अनुकूल होय म॑ असमर्थ होय जैतै । हुनका सब क॑ पता चललै कि जलवायु के कारण तापमान म॑ बदलाव के वजह स॑ २०५० तलक सालाना लगभग ४ लाख ३० हजार लोगऽ के मौत होय जैतै, जेकरा म॑ गरीब देशऽ म॑ अमीर देशऽ के तुलना म॑ १० गुना अधिक मौत केरऽ रिपोर्ट देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

नेपाल सहित ई फंसल क्षेत्रऽ म॑ ६७.६ करोड़ स॑ भी अधिक लोगऽ के रहना छै, आरू अध्ययन के अनुमान छै कि एकरऽ परिणामस्वरूप २०५० स॑ हर साल ई देशऽ म॑ लगभग ३ लाख ७७ हजार लोगऽ के जान जाय छै ।

पावर डाउन

नेपाल मे जलवायु प्रभाव के कारण प्रति व्यक्ति बिजली के खपत 0.01 जीजे के गिरावट आबि सकैत अछि, जाहि सं 32% आबादी के गर्मी के तनाव के सामना करय के क्षमता कम भ सकैत अछि. लोड-शेडिंग आ महग बिजली बहुत परिवार कए शीतलन उपकरण स वंचित क देत।

ई नेपाल के बिजली उत्पादन क्षमता 4300 मेगावाट तक पहुंचला के बावजूद. सरकार केरऽ योजना छै कि 2035 तलक 30,000 मेगावाट बिजली पैदा करलऽ जैतै, आरू 10,000-15,000 मेगावाट क॑ भारत आरू बांग्लादेश म॑ निर्यात करलऽ जैतै ।

शिकागो केरऽ ऊर्जा नीति संस्थान केरऽ सह-लेखक अश्विन रोड न॑ नोट करलकै कि नेपाल म॑ बिजली के खपत म॑ अनुमानित गिरावट जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण छै, आरू अन्य पैरामीटर प॑ नजर नै डालै छै ।

रोडे नेपाली टाइम्स स बातचीत मे कहलनि जे, नेपाल के बिजली उत्पादन के विस्तार शीतलन के समर्थन के लेल खपत बढ़ाबय के लक्ष्य के तरफ नीक खबर होयत। “लेकिन ई आंकड़ा के गणना अलग-अलग आय स्तर आरू जलवायु क्षेत्र मँ दैनिक तापमान आरू ऊर्जा के खपत के बीच अनुमानित संबंध के आधार प करलौ गेलौ छेलै।”

रिपोर्ट म॑ 18 मॉर्टलिटी कूलिंग ट्रैप देशऽ क॑ बिजली केरऽ पहुँच वाला आबादी के हिस्सा के हिसाब स॑ रैंकिंग देलऽ गेलऽ छै । १८ देशमे नेपालमे बांग्लादेशक बाद दोसर स्थानमे समग्र पहुँच अछि ।

जलवायु प्रवासन

‘मृत्यु शीतलन जाल’ मे एक देश के रूप मे सूचीबद्ध रहितो नेपाल के औसत ऊंचाई अपेक्षाकृत शीतल बना दैत अछि | सीमा पार सं पहाड़ दिस पलायन के अलावा नेपाल के भीतर लोक मैदान सं वापस पहाड़ पर चढ़य लागत.

संभावित जन पलायन के तैयारी के कमी छै, आ नीति जलवायु प्रवासन के त बाते छोड़ू, शमन आ अनुकूलन के संग तालमेल नहिं बैसा सकल अछि.

रोड चेतावनी दै छै: “जहाँ पलायन गर्म होय रहलऽ जलवायु के नुकसान स॑ बचै के तरीका पेश करै छै, वहीं ई एगो महंगा अनुकूलन रणनीति भी छै जे सबसें गरीब, सबसें कमजोर आबादी लेली विशेष रूप स॑ बोझिल होतै।”

शहरी गर्मी द्वीप

पंखा आरू एयर कंडीशनर स॑ ठंडा करला स॑ शहरी गर्मी द्वीप (यूएचआई) प्रभाव म॑ वृद्धि होय छै, जेकरा स॑ कोर शहर केरऽ केंद्र कम भीड़ वाला उपनगरऽ स॑ ५ डिग्री सेल्सियस तलक गरम होय जाय छै । गर्मी फंसय वाला कंक्रीट, डामर कें गहरे रंग कें सतह, वनस्पति कें कमी आ एयर कंडीशनिंग आ वाहन सं बेकार गर्मी यूएचआई मे वृद्धि करएयत छै (पृष्ठ 9)।

पहिने सं काठमांडू के रिंग रोड के भीतर शहर के कोर दिन में 4 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक आ सांझ में 3 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक बाहरी इलाका सं बेसी गरम रहैत अछि. हरियर-नीला रंगक स्थान तापमान कें 1.2 डिग्री सेल्सियस तइक कम कयर सकय छै.

दिलचस्प बात ई छै कि जहाँ 72% आबादी म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण बिजली के खपत म॑ अपेक्षाकृत छोटऽ बदलाव देखलऽ जाय के अनुमान छै, वहीं वू क्षेत्रऽ म॑ स॑ बहुत सारा क्षेत्रऽ म॑ जलवायु परिवर्तन के कारण मृत्यु दर म॑ काफी वृद्धि के अनुमान नै छै, कैन्हेंकि बहुत सारा क्षेत्र अधिक पहाड़ी क्षेत्रऽ म॑ छै, जहां ठंडा स॑ जुड़लऽ मौतऽ म॑ कमी गर्मी स॑ जुड़लऽ मौतऽ म॑ कोनो भी वृद्धि क॑ भरपाई करतै, ई बात के सह-लेखक एमिली ग्रोवर-कोपेक न॑ नोट करलकै रोडियम ग्रुप।

ऊर्जा : इम्प के मापन

अनुकूलन योजना कें लक्षित करय कें लेल मृत्यु दर पर बढ़ैत तापमान कें कार्य

एमिली ग्रोवर-कोपेक, अश्विन रोड, जेनेविव चमत्कार, माइकल ग्रीनस्टोन, टैमा कैरेटन

जुलाई २०२६

पलायन एकटा गरम विषय अछि

गैया विंस केरऽ २०२२ केरऽ किताब नोमाड सेंचुरी म॑ अनुमान लगैलऽ गेलऽ छै कि ३.५ अरब तक लोगऽ क॑ अबाध गर्मी स॑ प्रभावित होतै आरू वू हरकत म॑ ही रहतै । जन पलायन अनिवार्य अछि ताहि लेल सरकार के सेहो एहि विचार के आदत पड़ि सकैत अछि.

जूलियन हैटेम केरऽ शेल्टर फ्रॉम द स्टॉर्म: हाउ क्लाइमेट चेंज इज क्रिएटिंग ए न्यू एरा ऑफ माइग्रेशन (2026) म॑ नोट करलऽ गेलऽ छै कि गर्मी के कारण सामूहिक मानव विस्थापन पहल॑ स॑ ही होय रहलऽ छै आरू भविष्य केरऽ रुझान के साजिश रचै छै ।

केल्सी बेस्ट, कायली ओबर, आरू रॉबर्ट ए मैकलेमैन (2025) द्वारा बदलतऽ जलवायु म॑ प्रवास आरू विस्थापन न॑ ई जांच करलकै कि जलवायु परिवर्तन मानव समाज, बुनियादी ढाँचा, आरू क्षेत्रीय अनुकूलन उपायऽ के साथ कोना बातचीत करै छै ।

चाल : पराग खन्ना केरऽ ‘द फोर्सेस अपरूटिंग अस’ ई देखै छै कि लोग कोन-कोन देशऽ स॑ आबै वाला छै आरू जलवायु परिवर्तन केरऽ प्रभाव स॑ कत॑ बची सकै छै । भविष्य अव्यवस्थित रहत।

विज्ञान कथा लेखक किम स्टेनली रॉबिन्सन केरऽ २०१९ केरऽ उपन्यास द मिनिस्ट्री फॉर द फ्यूचर केरऽ शुरुआत उत्तरी भारत म॑ गर्मी के लहर के वजह स॑ दू करोड़ लोगऽ के सामूहिक मौत स॑ होय छै । मुदा विश्व सरकार अनुकूलन के वित्तपोषण के लेल एक संग आबि जाइत अछि.

title: Four bodies located after 10 climbers go missing on Pakistani peak - Al Jazeera

full_article:
The bodies of four climbers have reportedly been located by Pakistani search crews after at least 10 mountaineers went missing in a suspected avalanche on Broad Peak a ⁠day earlier, officials said.

Among those missing is Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja, also known as Nims Dai, who holds the record for the fastest ascent of the world’s 14 highest mountains, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said earlier.

Efforts were underway to retrieve the bodies of the four climbers despite the harsh weather on Friday, the Associated Press and Reuters news agencies reported, citing Pakistani sources. The AP said authorities did not identify whose bodies were found.

Sajid Hussain, the deputy director of the tourism department in Pakistan’s Gilgit-Baltistan region, told Reuters the search for the remaining six was focusing on a “remote and difficult area”.

Broad Peak is the 12th-highest mountain in the world.

The 10 climbers, led by Purja, went missing after an avalanche in northern Pakistan where they were on a climbing expedition, the ACP said late on Thursday.

“The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) has received deeply concerning reports of an avalanche that struck a team of climbers on Broad Peak (8,047m) in the Karakoram mountain range,” the club said in a statement.

It said the expedition comprised of 10 people, including five Nepali climbers, Pakistani mountaineer Sohail Sakhi from Hunza, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified only as Wang, and another foreign climber whose nationality it did not disclose.

“The entire team has reportedly been out of communication since the avalanche,” the club said.

“Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” it added.

Purja, 43, has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide in 2018, after leaving the British military.

He climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders” (peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet) in six months and six days between April and October 2019, a record at the time.

In 2021, Purja completed the first winter ascent of K2 as part of a team of nine other Nepalese climbers.

अधिकारी सब कहलनि जे, एक ⁠दिन पहिने ब्रॉड पीक पर संदिग्ध हिमस्खलन में कम सं कम दस पर्वतारोही के लापता भेला के बाद पाकिस्तानी खोज दल द्वारा चारि टा पर्वतारोही के लाश के पता लगाओल गेल अछि.

लापता लोगऽ म॑ नेपाली पर्वतारोही निर्मल पुर्जा भी शामिल छै, जेकरा निम्स दाई के नाम स॑ भी जानलऽ जाय छै, जेकरा पास दुनिया केरऽ १४ सबसें ऊँचऽ पहाड़ऽ म॑ सबसें तेज चढ़ै के रिकॉर्ड छै, ई बात स॑ पहल॑ पाकिस्तान केरऽ अल्पाइन क्लब (एसीपी) न॑ कहल॑ छेलै ।

पाकिस्तानी सूत्र के हवाला स॑ एसोसिएटेड प्रेस आरू रायटर समाचार एजेंसी न॑ बतैलकै कि शुक्रवार क॑ कठोर मौसम के बावजूद चारो पर्वतारोही के शव क॑ बरामद करै के कोशिश चलैलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै । एपी कहलनि जे, अधिकारी केकर लाश भेटल अछि, एकर पहचान नहि केलक अछि।

पाकिस्तान केरऽ गिलगित-बाल्तिस्तान क्षेत्र केरऽ पर्यटन विभाग केरऽ उप निदेशक साजिद हुसैन न॑ रायटर क॑ बतैलकै कि बाकी छह लोगऽ के खोज एगो “दूरस्थ आरू कठिन क्षेत्र” प॑ केंद्रित छै ।

ब्रॉड पीक विश्वक १२म सबसँ ऊँच पहाड़ छी ।

गुरुवार देर रात एसीपी नँ कहलकै कि पूर्वा के नेतृत्व मँ ई १० पर्वतारोही उत्तरी पाकिस्तान मँ हिमस्खलन के बाद लापता होय गेलौ छै, जहां हुनी पर्वतारोही अभियान मँ छेलै ।

क्लब न॑ जारी बयान म॑ कहलकै कि अल्पाइन क्लब आफ पाकिस्तान (एसीपी) क॑ काराकोरम पर्वत श्रृंखला केरऽ ब्रॉड पीक (८,०४७ मीटर) प॑ पर्वतारोही के टीम प॑ हिमस्खलन के गहराई स॑ चिंताजनक खबर मिललऽ छै ।

ओ कहलक जे एहि अभियान मे 10 गोटे शामिल छथि, जाहि मे पांचटा नेपाली पर्वतारोही, हुन्जा क पाकिस्तानी पर्वतारोही सोहेल सखी, ओमानी पर्वतारोही नाथिरा, अमेरिकी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस, चीनी पर्वतारोही मैलोरी गेस, जेकर पहचान केवल वांग क नाम स अछि, आ एकटा आओर विदेशी पर्वतारोही जिनकर राष्ट्रीयता क खुलासा नहि कैल गेल अछि।

विज्ञापन

क्लब कहलनि जे, हिमस्खलन के बाद सं पूरा टीम के संवाद सं बाहर भ गेल अछि।

एकरा म॑ आरू कहलऽ गेलऽ छै कि मौसम आरू परिचालन केरऽ स्थिति के आधार प॑ हेलीकॉप्टर केरऽ सहायता आरू सब उपलब्ध बचाव संसाधन क॑ जल्दी स॑ जल्दी मौका प॑ जुटाबै के हर संभव प्रयास करलऽ जाय रहलऽ छै ।

43 वर्षीय पुर्जा ब्रिटिश सेना छोड़लाक बाद 2018 मे पूर्णकालिक पर्वतारोही आ टूर गाइड बनलाक बाद सं कईटा पर्वतारोहण रिकॉर्ड तोड़ि चुकल छथि।

अप्रैल आरू अक्टूबर २०१९ के बीच छह महीना आरू छह दिन म॑ हुनी सब १४ “आठ-हजार” (८,००० मीटर स॑ ऊपर के चोटी, यानी २६,००० फीट) प॑ चढ़ी गेलै, जे कि वू समय के रिकॉर्ड छेलै ।
